topics.label: Human Body Systems
facts: Your body is made of systems that work together, like the circulatory, respiratory, digestive, and nervous systems.
The circulatory system uses the heart and blood vessels to carry oxygen and nutrients around the body.
The respiratory system takes in oxygen when you breathe in and removes carbon dioxide when you breathe out.
The nervous system uses the brain, spinal cord, and nerves to send messages around the body very quickly.

questions.q: Which system carries oxygen and nutrients around the body?
questions.fact: The heart pumps blood through vessels, carrying oxygen and nutrients to every cell.

questions.q: Which system takes in oxygen when you breathe?
questions.fact: The respiratory system includes the lungs, where oxygen enters the blood.

questions.q: What is the control centre of the nervous system?
questions.fact: The brain receives messages from nerves and tells the body what to do.

questions.q: Which two systems work together to break down food and deliver its nutrients?
questions.fact: The digestive system breaks food down, and the blood carries the nutrients around the body.

topics.label: Cells
facts: Cells are the smallest units of life, and all living things are made of them.
The nucleus is the part of a cell that controls it and holds the instructions for life.
Plant cells have a cell wall and chloroplasts, which animal cells do not have.
Mitochondria are the parts of a cell that release energy from food.

questions.fact: All living things, from tiny bacteria to blue whales, are made of cells.

questions.q: Which part of the cell controls it and holds the instructions for life?
questions.fact: The nucleus holds DNA, the instructions that tell the cell what to do.

questions.q: Which part of a cell releases energy from food?
questions.fact: Mitochondria release energy from food in respiration, so they are called the powerhouse of the cell.

questions.q: Which of these do plant cells have but animal cells do not?
questions.fact: Chloroplasts trap sunlight for photosynthesis, and only plant cells have them.

topics.label: Digestion
facts: Digestion is the process of breaking food down into tiny nutrients your body can use.
Digestion starts in the mouth, where teeth chew food and saliva starts to break it down.
The stomach churns food and mixes it with acid and enzymes.
In the small intestine, nutrients pass into the blood, which carries them around the body.

choices: Breaking food down into nutrients the body can use
questions.fact: Digestion turns food into tiny nutrients that can pass into the blood.
Teeth chew food and saliva begins breaking it down before you even swallow.

choices: It churns food and mixes it with acid and enzymes
questions.fact: The stomach's acid and churning turn food into a thick soup.

questions.q: Where do nutrients pass into the blood?
questions.fact: The small intestine absorbs nutrients through its walls into the bloodstream.

topics.label: The Heart and Blood
facts: Your heart is a muscle about the size of your fist, and it pumps blood around your whole body.
The heart has four chambers: two atria on top and two ventricles below.
Red blood cells carry oxygen from your lungs to every part of your body.
Blood travels through three kinds of vessels: arteries, veins, and tiny capillaries.

choices: It pumps blood around your body
questions.fact: The heart is a muscle that pumps blood around the body.

questions.q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.fact: The heart has four chambers: two atria and two ventricles.

questions.q: What do red blood cells carry?
choices: Carbon dioxide to the lungs only
questions.fact: Red blood cells pick up oxygen in the lungs and deliver it around the body.

questions.q: Which vessels carry blood away from the heart?
questions.fact: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, while veins carry it back.
